name: Hearing (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Systematic study of the Upaniṣads (with the Gītā and Brahma Sūtras) under a qualified teacher, determining by the six marks of purport that their meaning is the non-dual Brahman; for the Vivaraṇa the principal means, for one of sharp understanding sufficient by itself.
signs_of_progress: doubt about what scripture teaches is removed (pramāṇa-saṃśaya)

name: Reflection (manana)
method_summary: Continuous reasoning in harmony with the teaching to remove doubts about the object (whether the self can be Brahman), meeting objections by reasoning that does not oppose scripture.

name: Contemplation (nididhyāsana)
method_summary: A continuous flow of the thought of the self as Brahman, excluding contrary ideas, to remove the deep-rooted habit of identifying with body and mind; culminates in (savikalpa and nirvikalpa) samādhi; for the Bhāmatī the principal means, making mediate knowledge direct.

name: Self-inquiry (ātma-vicāra)
method_summary: Inquiring 'Who am I? How did this world arise? Who is its maker? What is its material?' and discriminating the self from all that is seen; inquiry, not action, attains the Real.

name: Negation: 'not this, not this' (neti neti)
method_summary: Negating every object, attribute and adjunct as not the self ('I am not the body, senses, mind…'), until only the undeniable witnessing consciousness remains; the negation is of specifications, not of Brahman.

name: Abiding as the witness (sākṣi-bhāva)
method_summary: Recognizing oneself as the unchanging witness of the mind's modes, the senses and the states, like the lamp in a theatre that lights all and remains when all have gone.

name: Discrimination of seer and seen (dṛg-dṛśya-viveka)
method_summary: Tracing the chain of seer and seen — object seen by eye, eye by mind, mind by witness — to the seer that is never seen.

name: Discrimination of the five sheaths (pañca-kośa-viveka)
method_summary: Examining each sheath in turn — food, vital air, mind, intellect, bliss — as changing and known, hence not the self, until the self as their witness and support is recognized.

name: Analysis of the three states (avasthā-traya-viveka)
method_summary: Observing that waking, dream and sleep and their objects come and go while the consciousness that knows them is uniform and continuous, and identifying with that consciousness.

name: Method of agreement and difference (anvaya-vyatireka)
method_summary: Reasoning that what persists when other things are absent (consciousness through the states) is distinct from what is absent when it persists (body, senses, mind); used by Sureśvara to separate self from not-self.

name: Discrimination of the eternal and the non-eternal
method_summary: Cultivating the firm conviction that Brahman alone is eternal and real and all else transient; the first of the four qualifications.

name: Cultivation of the six virtues (ṣaṭ-sampatti)
method_summary: Practising calm, self-control, withdrawal, forbearance, faith and concentration as auxiliaries of knowledge (BS 3.4.27; BĀU 4.4.23).

name: Parisaṃkhyāna meditation (Upadeśasāhasrī)
method_summary: Reviewing each object of the senses as not-self and changing and oneself as pure, unrelated, changeless awareness, so as to cease identifying with them and to stop generating merit and demerit.

name: Prasaṅkhyāna (repeated contemplation after verbal knowledge)
method_summary: In Maṇḍana's view, repeatedly contemplating the knowledge obtained from the Upaniṣads until it becomes direct and destroys the impressions of difference; regarded as unnecessary for the fully qualified by Śaṅkara (US 18) and Sureśvara.

name: Asparśa-yoga ('contactless' yoga)
method_summary: Gauḍapāda's discipline: realizing the unborn, controlling the mind without weariness (like emptying the ocean with a blade of grass), rousing it from dullness, calming distraction, recognizing latent attachment, not disturbing equilibrium, not relishing the bliss, until the mind becomes no-mind.

warnings.text: Yogins fear it, seeing fear in the fearless.
One should not relish the happiness arising in it; relishing is an obstacle.

signs_of_progress: the mind no longer imagines; no-mind (GK 3.32)

name: Meditation on Oṃ (praṇava-upāsanā)
method_summary: Fixing the mind on Oṃ, whose sounds a, u, m correspond to waking, dream and sleep and whose soundless 'fourth' to turīya; Oṃ is the fearless Brahman.

name: Meditation on the qualified Brahman (saguṇa-upāsanā)
method_summary: Sustained meditation on Brahman with attributes or through a symbol (Oṃ, the sun, the mind), seated, one-pointed, in any suitable place, continued until death; leads to the Brahma-world and gradual liberation, and prepares the mind for knowledge.

name: Meditation on the attributeless (nirguṇa-upāsanā)
method_summary: For those unable to inquire: meditating on the attributeless Brahman as 'I am Brahman', which, like following a gem's light, leads to knowledge; also separating being–shining–dear from name and form in all things.

name: Savikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption with the mental mode resting in Brahman while the distinction of knower and known remains; with inner and outer forms, attended by objects or by words (Dṛg-Dṛśya Viveka).

warnings.text: Relishing its bliss (rasāsvāda) obstructs nirvikalpa samādhi.

name: Nirvikalpa samādhi (Vedānta)
method_summary: Absorption in which the mode in the form of Brahman remains without distinction of knower and known, like salt dissolved in water; its eight auxiliaries are the yoga limbs and its obstacles dullness, distraction, latent attachment and relishing.

warnings.text: Four obstacles: laya, vikṣepa, kaṣāya, rasāsvāda.

name: Destruction of latent tendencies (vāsanā-kṣaya)
method_summary: Weakening impure tendencies (attachment, pride, the three vāsanās) by cultivating their opposites and pure tendencies, until even these are let go; practised with knowledge and dissolution of mind.

name: Dissolution of the mind (mano-nāśa)
method_summary: Bringing the mind to cease from forming modes, through yoga and dispassion, for the stable enjoyment of liberation while living.

name: Renunciation of the seeker (vividiṣā-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Formal renunciation of rites and possessions by one who desires knowledge, to devote oneself wholly to hearing and the rest.

name: Renunciation of the knower (vidvat-sannyāsa)
method_summary: Renunciation by one who has attained knowledge, as the natural expression and protection of liberation while living (the paramahaṃsa life).

name: Performance of obligatory duties for purification
method_summary: Performing the daily and occasional rites and one's duties without desire for their fruits, offered to the Lord, avoiding desire-prompted and forbidden acts, for the purification of mind that makes one fit for knowledge.

name: Approaching the teacher (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: Approaching, 'fuel in hand', a teacher learned in scripture and established in Brahman, with humility, service and questioning, and receiving the teaching repeatedly until it is grasped.

name: Dwelling on one's own nature (svasvarūpānusandhāna) as devotion
method_summary: Devotion understood as continuous attention to one's own true nature (VC 31), the chief among the means to liberation.

name: Practice of Brahman (brahmābhyāsa)
method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, instructing one another in it, and being wholly devoted to it — the constant practice recommended after knowledge dawns (quoted in the Pañcadaśī from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha).

name: Worship of the five deities (pañcāyatana-pūjā)
method_summary: Domestic worship of Śiva, Viṣṇu, Devī, Sūrya and Gaṇeśa (one at the centre as the chosen deity), which the Smārta tradition credits Śaṅkara with systematizing; worship of the qualified Brahman for purification and devotion.
notes: Tradition's account; the attribution to Śaṅkara is not supported by his accepted works.
